designDirection: New single continuous armored hull with one broad prow; replaces the rejected three-pronged concept.

prompts.step: Generate new single-hull Titan five-view sheet
prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a NEW five-view 2D orthographic modeling reference sheet for the TITAN flagship in Stellar Syndicates.

Primary request: Design an entirely NEW Titan spaceship. The user dislikes the old three-headed / three-pronged Titan. Replace that visual idea completely with ONE continuous, imposing armored hull and ONE broad central prow. Create exactly five complete views of this same new ship: FRONT, BACK, TOP, BOTTOM, and SIDE.

Design direction: a monumental fortress battleship with a single solid shield-shaped wedge hull, very broad armored shoulders, a powerful chisel-point bow, a wide integrated stern, and layered armor terraces. One uninterrupted silhouette; the forward third tapers smoothly from the full-width body to ONE bluntly pointed bow, with no long thin neck. About 2.1 times as long as its maximum width. A compact low command citadel is embedded on the centerline of the aft third, not a tall skyscraper bridge. A deep recessed central spinal weapon channel is integrated into the bow armor without splitting the prow into separate prongs. Three pairs of substantial, low-profile twin-barrel turrets lie along the dorsal left and right shoulders, with all barrels pointing forward. Recessed side hangar doors sit INSIDE the continuous hull, below the shoulder armor; they must not look like separate pods or extra ship heads. Fine maintenance hatches, narrow windows, small sensors, radiator banks, structural ribs, and dense but legible panel seams convey flagship scale. No giant fighter cockpit. No external cargo containers. This should feel like a coherent massive flagship with simple strong primary forms and finely detailed surfaces.

Single-hull rule: NO trident, NO three heads, NO forked prow, NO separated forward arms, NO forward outriggers, NO detached side hulls, NO long open channels between hull branches, NO giant wing spikes. The entire nose is ONE solid connected wedge. The silhouette must read as one ship rather than a cluster of three ships.

Engines: exactly SIX large circular stern exhaust nozzles in ONE horizontal row, integrated into a continuous armored stern block. All six point directly rearward. Their locations must agree in every view. No extra auxiliary engines, no vertical stacks, no detached engine nacelles. Layered dark metal nozzle rims, restrained cyan interiors, no exhaust plumes.

Family style: original premium sci-fi hard-surface design for the same game as the previous ships. Pale titanium and off-white armor, dark charcoal structural metal, restrained brass edging and fasteners, small cyan light strips, clear panel seams and mild surface wear. Elegant clean industrial spacecraft construction, with broad readable armor slabs. Fully colored technical concept illustration, crisp charcoal outlines, gentle neutral shading, high detail without excessive tiny clutter. No dramatic beauty-render lighting.

Sheet layout: wide LANDSCAPE approximately 2:1 aspect ratio, high native resolution. Clean warm-white background. TOP and BOTTOM are the two large views on the left, both nose straight UP, exactly matching length and beam. FRONT sits at the upper right, BACK at middle right, and a long SIDE elevation at lower right with nose pointing LEFT. All complete with comfortable margins and no overlap. Side length corresponds to plan-view length. Front and back widths correspond to plan-view beam. Give the two large plan views ample room for the broad single hull.
Exact text only: title "TITAN", and five simple labels "TOP", "BOTTOM", "FRONT", "BACK", "SIDE" beneath the appropriate views. No other text, no dimensions.

Projection requirements:
TOP: true straight overhead orthographic. Show the ONE broad wedge, continuous closed armored shoulders, low command citadel, six turret mounts in three mirrored pairs, and six rearward engine housings. Engine axes run fore-aft, with only thin rear lip edges visible overhead, not upward-facing round exhaust discs.
BOTTOM: true straight underneath, nose UP. Exactly the same one-piece exterior outline, beam, length and six engine positions as TOP. A genuinely distinct, fully textured underside: layered belly armor, central protected keel, inset rectangular maintenance and docking hatches, thermal panels, recessed piping and radiator strips, brass access catches and tiny cyan service lights. No copied dorsal turrets or command tower. No landing legs. Finish the entire underside to the edges.
FRONT: exact level head-on orthographic elevation, zero camera elevation. The fore-aft length collapses. Show a wide shallow armored hull, one low central chisel-bow cross section, shoulder armor and small turret barrel ends where not occluded, with the modest aft command citadel rising behind. No long spear sticking upward, no overhead surfaces viewed from above, no rear engine circles through the hull.
BACK: exact level stern-on orthographic, matching FRONT width and height. Exactly SIX round cyan main exhaust apertures in a single horizontal row in the stern block. Show the backs of forward-facing turret housings, not gun muzzle holes facing backward. No extra engines.
SIDE: true level orthographic side elevation, bow LEFT and engines RIGHT. Consistent single hull with a long low armored sidewall, restrained tiered dorsal deck, one compact aft command citadel, three corresponding near-side forward-pointing turrets and recessed hangar doors. Real layered belly geometry. Longitudinal engine housing at right; the other five nozzles are across the width and occlude naturally, not stacked vertically. No three-quarter perspective.

All five views must describe the same NEW single-hull ship, with consistent major armor divisions, turret positions, command citadel, engine layout, thickness and silhouette. Avoid extra hero views, inset drawings, comparison ships, starfields, scenery, grids over the artwork, logos, watermarks, dramatic shadows, smoke, and any return to the old three-pronged design.
